assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period compared: 18-31 Oct 2026 versus 4-17 Oct 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Attempt volume 18-31 Oct was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. Sales and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period; it is flagged for context, not treated as an error.
Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 88.5%, order-level 90.9%, technical 92.1%. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts, not as shares of failures.
The daily success-rate series provided covers only part of the window, so the exact start date of the drop is not pinned down here.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% to 88.5% (about 230,100 attempts in the last 14 days vs 165,297 in the prior 14). The drop is statistically and practically significant.
By payment method, the mix effect was -1.00pp and the like-for-like rate effect was -0.47pp, so mix explains about 68.0% of the drop.

CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 10.9% of attempts while its own success rate was flat (81.7% to 81.6%). It contributed -0.62pp, almost all from mix. UPI's share fell from 54.0% to 42.5% at an unchanged 93.0% success rate.
NovaMart grew from 6.0% to 30.0% of attempts and its success rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%. It accounts for -0.96pp (65.3%) of the -1.47pp change.

Within the like-for-like effect, the biggest single pocket is Harbor Bank debit cards: success fell from 86.2% to 76.7% (-9.44pp), contributing -0.39pp. Overall, debit card success fell 2.65pp from 86.0% to 83.4%; other payment methods did not move significantly.

For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts (22 to 1,065 failures). Other failure codes for this segment each moved by roughly 0.3 per 100 attempts or less.
Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
Attempt volume rose about 39% versus the usual level for these weekdays over 18-31 Oct. Daily success rates in the first 12 days of the baseline stayed around 89.4%-90.4%.
The drop is visible under all three definitions in the last 14 days: attempt-level 88.5%, order-level 90.9%, technical 92.1%.

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp, from 90.0% to 88.5%. About two-thirds of that (-1.00pp) is a payment-mix shift toward lower-success methods like EMI, and the rest (-0.47pp) is a like-for-like drop, concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the campaign calendar and NovaMart's payment-method mix before and after 18 Oct; recompute the rate with a fixed mix.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's share rose from 6.0% to 30.0% at the same time as the +39% volume spike and CARD_EMI's share rising from 2.9% to 10.9%, while EMI and UPI success rates themselves were flat.
hypotheses.text: A sale or campaign (NovaMart-led) from 18 Oct pushed volume up and shifted traffic toward EMI and credit cards and away from UPI, lowering the blended rate through mix rather than a like-for-like decline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk or velocity rules changed after 17 Oct, and check whether the declines cluster on specific merchants, amounts or cards.
hypotheses.rationale: Harbor Bank debit success fell 9.44pp and ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE jumped from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts while other codes barely moved.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened or misfired its risk rules on debit cards during the high-volume period, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break NovaMart's attempts down by payment method and issuer and compare against other merchants on the same method.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart is the top segment on both share growth and rate decline, but the evidence does not isolate its payment-method or issuer breakdown.
hypotheses.text: NovaMart's own success rate decline (90.0% to 86.2%) may reflect the type of traffic it brought (more EMI, more risk-flagged debit cards) rather than a problem on its side.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened or misfired its risk rules on debit cards during the high-volume period, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE.
recommendations.rationale: This is the largest identified like-for-like loss and has one dominant failure code.
recommendations.text: Contact Harbor Bank about the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike on debit cards and request a review or whitelist of legitimate traffic.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A sale or campaign (NovaMart-led) from 18 Oct pushed volume up and shifted traffic toward EMI and credit cards and away from UPI, lowering the blended rate through mix rather than a like-for-like decline.
recommendations.rationale: 68.0% of the drop is mix, not a deterioration within payment methods.
recommendations.text: Report success rate on a mix-adjusted basis (or by payment method) during sales so that mix shifts are not read as performance declines.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
recommendations.rationale: These codes increased alongside the EMI growth and are candidates for recoverable failures.
recommendations.text: Review EMI eligibility checks and 3DS flows, since EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE and AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED both rose per 100 attempts as EMI volume grew.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: NovaMart's own success rate decline (90.0% to 86.2%) may reflect the type of traffic it brought (more EMI, more risk-flagged debit cards) rather than a problem on its side.
recommendations.rationale: NovaMart explains 65.3% of the change, so targeted fixes there have the most leverage.
recommendations.text: Break NovaMart's performance down by payment method and issuer to see whether its 3.8pp lower rate is specific to certain segments.
